headline: Homemade Honey Wheat Sandwich Bread, Start to Finish
tldr: Follow this step-by-step method and you'll turn flour, honey, and butter into a tender, bakery-style sandwich loaf at home.
summary: Charlie walks through making honey wheat sandwich bread from scratch, starting by combining whole wheat flour and bread flour (or all-purpose) with warm water in a stand mixer. An optional 30-minute autolyse rest lets the flour's starches break down, which jump-starts gluten development before any kneading happens.

After the rest, instant yeast, honey, brown sugar, and salt get stirred in, and the dough is kneaded for 10 minutes with a dough hook to build the bulk of its gluten structure. Softened butter is then worked in gradually over another 5 minutes rather than added earlier, since fat coating the flour too soon would hinder gluten formation. A deliberately small amount of yeast slows the rise, which helps the dough develop deeper flavor.

The dough rises until doubled in size (45 minutes to an hour), then gets punched down to release gas before shaping. Using a metal bench scraper and a fold-and-tuck technique, the dough is worked into a tight rectangle-turned-loaf, with surface bubbles popped and the loaf dragged across the counter to build tension and seal the seams.

The shaped loaf goes seam-down into a greased 9x5 pan for its final rise until it fills the pan, then gets brushed with egg wash and topped with kosher salt and optional rolled oats, dropped from height for even coverage. It bakes at 350°F for 25-30 minutes, gets tented with foil to stop further browning, and returns to the oven for 15 more minutes to finish cooking through.

Once baked, the loaf cools on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing, since the interior keeps cooking as it cools. The result is a tender, slightly sweet honey wheat sandwich bread built entirely from simple, weighed ingredients.
mindmap:
# Honey Wheat Sandwich Bread

## Dough Ingredients
- Whole wheat flour 165g
- Bread flour or all-purpose 255g
  - Bread flour has more gluten
  - Gives nicer chew
- Warm water 270g at 100°F
- Instant yeast 4g
- Honey 32g
- Brown sugar 36g
- Salt 10g
- Unsalted butter 42g, softened

## Mixing Process
- Combine flours and water
- Optional autolyse rest 30 minutes
  - Breaks down starches
  - Jump-starts gluten development
- Add yeast, honey, sugar, salt
- Knead 10 minutes with dough hook
- Add butter gradually
  - Added late to protect gluten
- Knead 5 more minutes

## Bulk Fermentation
- Shape into a ball, cover
- Rise until doubled, 45min-1hr
  - Slower rise builds more flavor
  - Small yeast amount slows rise

## Shaping the Loaf
- Punch down to degas
- Dust surface, leave top unfloured
- Fold into tight rectangle
  - Fold near side to middle
  - Fold left and right sides
  - Fold far corners, tuck
- Pop surface bubbles
- Drag loaf to build tension

## Final Proof and Bake Prep
- Place seam-down in greased 9x5 pan
- Rise until dough fills pan
- Preheat oven to 350°F
- Brush with egg wash
- Sprinkle kosher salt and oats

## Baking
- Bake 25-30 minutes until golden
- Tent with foil
- Bake 15 more minutes
- Cool on wire rack 30 min minimum

stickies.text: Why would you buy bread at store when you can just make it yourself?
A small amount of yeast slows the rise, which lets the dough develop even more flavor.
Butter is added after kneading, not before, because it hinders gluten development.
Leave the top of the dough unfloured so it can stick to itself while shaping.
Dropping oats and salt from high up isn't just for looks — it actually distributes them more evenly.
Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes, then 15 more minutes tented with foil.
Wait at least half an hour before cutting in — the inside is still finishing cooking as it cools.
There's your beautiful, tender and slightly sweet honey wheat sandwich bread.

receipts.title: Autolyse rests the dough before kneading
receipts.detail: Letting the mixed flour and water sit for 30 minutes breaks down starches and jump-starts gluten development, which helps a lot even before kneading starts, especially with all-purpose flour.

receipts.title: Small yeast amount slows the rise on purpose
receipts.detail: Using only 4 grams of instant yeast makes the dough rise more slowly, which lets it develop deeper flavor as it ferments.

receipts.title: Butter goes in after kneading, never before
receipts.detail: Fat coats flour and blocks gluten strands from forming, so the softened butter is worked in only after 10 minutes of kneading has already built the dough's structure.

receipts.title: Leave the dough's top bare for shaping
receipts.detail: Flouring the work surface but keeping the top of the dough unfloured lets it grip itself during the fold-and-tuck sequence, producing a tighter final loaf.

receipts.title: Fold, tuck, and drag to build tension
receipts.detail: Working the dough into a rectangle, folding the corners under repeatedly, and dragging the loaf across the counter closes the seams and builds the surface tension needed for a good oven rise.

receipts.title: Egg wash before baking adds shine and color
receipts.detail: Brushing the risen loaf with one egg beaten with a teaspoon of water gives the crust a nice shine and helps it turn a deeper golden brown.

receipts.title: Drop toppings from height for even coverage
receipts.detail: Sprinkling rolled oats and kosher salt from high above the loaf spreads them more evenly than sprinkling up close, the same trick chefs use when salting food.

receipts.title: Tenting with foil stops over-browning mid-bake
receipts.detail: Once the crust hits the desired color partway through baking, tenting the loaf with foil prevents further browning while the interior keeps cooking for another 15 minutes.

receipts.title: Let the loaf cool before slicing it
receipts.detail: The bread's interior is still finishing cooking as it cools, so cutting in before at least 30 minutes have passed risks a gummy, underbaked crumb.

moves: Weigh out 165g whole wheat flour and 255g bread flour on a kitchen scale before starting.
Use the oven light (or a warm spot) to hold dough around 85°F during both rises.
Pick up a metal bench scraper to keep the dough from sticking while shaping.
Bake at 350°F and tent with foil once golden so the crust doesn't over-brown.
Let the finished loaf cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

steps.text: Combine whole wheat flour, bread flour, and warm water in the mixer bowl.
Let the dough autolyse (rest) 30 minutes to develop gluten.
Add instant yeast, honey, brown sugar, and salt; stir until incorporated.
Knead with the dough hook for 10 minutes to build gluten.
Add softened butter gradually, then knead 5 more minutes.
Shape dough into a ball, cover, and let rise until doubled.
Punch down the risen dough to release the gas.
Shape dough into a rectangle, fold into a tight loaf, and tuck the seams.
Place the loaf seam-down in a greased 9x5 pan for the final rise.
Brush the risen loaf with egg wash; sprinkle with kosher salt and optional oats.
Tent with foil and bake 15 more minutes to finish cooking.
Cool on a wire rack at least 30 minutes before slicing.
